cases.customer_question: Can a Bluetooth HID keyboard qualify successfully if HOGP passes but BAS, DIS, and HIDS-related tests fail or are inconclusive?
question_variants: Do failed BAS/DIS/HIDS tests block Bluetooth qualification?
Is HOGP qualification alone sufficient for a HID keyboard?
Why did HOGP pass but qualification still fail?
Do HOGP HID devices need BAS, DIS, and HIDS support?
Can we obtain certification with Fail or Indecisive PTS results?
cases.actual_issue: The product implemented HOGP based on a legacy design, but mandatory supporting profile functionality required for HOGP HID devices was not fully implemented, causing BAS, DIS, and HIDS PTS failures.
cases.plain_english_explanation: The keyboard successfully passed the HOGP-specific tests, but additional Bluetooth profile features that are now required for HOGP HID devices were missing. Because those required features were not implemented, several mandatory qualification tests failed or produced inconclusive results. Passing only the main HID profile tests is not enough when dependent profile requirements apply.
cases.consultant_answer: For HOGP HID devices, support for BAS, DIS, and HIDS became required under the applicable qualification requirements. Testing showed that HOGP itself passed, but mandatory BAS, DIS, and HIDS items failed because required information and functionality such as Battery Level and PnP ID were not implemented. The likely cause was reuse of an older profile implementation that matched previous qualification expectations but not the newer requirements. The development team should review the PTS logs, verify implementation coverage, add the missing functionality, and retest.
cases.decision_logic: Qualification is based on passing all applicable mandatory requirements generated by the selected profile and ICS configuration. When HOGP qualification requires BAS, DIS, and HIDS support, missing mandatory functionality in those dependent profiles prevents successful completion even if the HOGP-specific tests pass.
cases.final_recommendation: Review the PTS failure logs, implement the missing BAS, DIS, and HIDS requirements, update the product implementation as needed, and rerun the failed qualification tests before proceeding with qualification submission.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: The product may be unable to complete Bluetooth qualification because mandatory test cases remain failed or inconclusive. This can lead to retesting, engineering rework, and qualification delays.
